name: vat adversarial corpus
description: Documented hostile inputs for a parser, validator, or AI agent that reads this format, each with the safe expected behaviour.

cases.title: CRLF into the VIES subrequest
cases.expected: Reject control characters before building the VIES request; never echo the value into a header.
cases.rationale: VIES validation makes an outbound call — CRLF can inject headers into it.

cases.title: SSRF via a URL-shaped VAT number
cases.expected: Reject: a VAT number is a country prefix plus a national pattern, never a URL.
cases.rationale: If the value is used to build a lookup URL, an attacker can target the cloud metadata endpoint.

cases.title: SQL injection in the VAT field
cases.expected: Reject on structure; parameterise any query.
cases.rationale: Same class as the IBAN case, on the VAT path.

cases.title: Template expression in the VAT field
cases.expected: Reject on structure; do not evaluate untrusted values.
cases.rationale: Template injection if the value is rendered server-side.

cases.title: Log forging in the VAT field
cases.expected: Reject control characters; escape before logging.

cases.title: Cyrillic homoglyph in the country prefix
cases.expected: Reject: the prefix must be ASCII A-Z.
cases.rationale: Homoglyph prefixes defeat registry lookups and case-folding.

cases.title: Null byte in the VAT field
cases.rationale: Truncation can hide trailing content from one layer and not another.

cases.title: Oversized VAT number
cases.expected: Reject on the national length rule before any external lookup.
cases.rationale: Bounds the cost of the check and the outbound request.

cases.title: Unregistered country prefix
cases.rationale: A validator must not fall back to a permissive default.

cases.title: Greece is EL, not GR
cases.expected: Reject or normalise to EL, per VIES. Document the choice.
cases.rationale: Greece uses the EL prefix for VAT; GR is the ISO country code, not the VAT prefix.
